title: Reservation and Transportation Ticket Agents and Travel Clerks

tasks.short: Build travel options, check availability and connections, calculate total prices and prepare an itinerary for customer approval.

steps.what: Discuss dates, budget, destinations, accommodation needs and travel preferences with the customer.
Search transport schedules and accommodation inventory in the reservation system.
Check missing accommodation or transport options through supplier portals.
Compute fares, taxes, ancillary charges and fees in the reservation system.
Weigh connection times, location, accessibility and cancellation terms to select suitable options.
Assemble the itinerary, itemised price, conditions and quote expiry.
Explain the quote and confirm the customer's preferred itinerary.

tasks.design: Configure search and pricing in the reservation system in {OTHER}, adding deterministic adapters for supported {PARTNER_PORTAL} inventory and checks for connection times, currencies and quote expiry. A deterministic generator produces the itemised itinerary in {DOCS}; the agent handles difficult trade-offs, and customer acceptance is recorded in the {WORKFLOW} before a separate booking action.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful search and pricing engines already existed, but supplier coverage and quote assembly were fragmented. Integration access and fare-rule exceptions made custom stitching expensive.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing search and pricing can be reused rather than rebuilt. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of adapters, validation rules and document generation.
tasks.still_hard: Live inventory changes, protected versus separate-ticket connections and nonstandard fees complicate comparisons. Supplier interfaces and accessibility information may be incomplete.
tasks.human_edge: Understand which inconvenience the customer will accept and spot an itinerary that is technically valid but unsuitable.

ambition.what: An accessible multi-leg itinerary comparison with total prices and connection trade-offs.

tasks.altitude: The agent spends less time searching supplier screens and assembling quotes, and more time comparing meaningful alternatives. Booking and spending authority stay unchanged; any delegated exception limits need supervisor agreement.

reach.task: Explain itinerary changes and alternative travel options after disruption.
reach.learn: Learn fare restrictions, separate-ticket risks and customer communication during disruption.

reach.role: First-Line Supervisor of Office and Administrative Support Workers
reach.task: Set escalation thresholds for risky connections and unusual quote conditions.
reach.learn: Learn service economics, supplier constraints and exception approval limits.

evidence.claim: Route filtering, fare calculations and itinerary generation can use deterministic rules and existing reservation engines.
Exact imports orders and synchronises stock. This supports structured integration as a pattern, not travel inventory or fare coverage.
Rossum validates extracted order data against business rules and routes exceptions to people. Travel quotes still need their own fare and inventory checks.

assumptions: The company uses a reservation system in {OTHER} and supplier portals for inventory outside its main coverage.
Existing pricing features cover standard fares, taxes and fees; uncovered charges are flagged rather than guessed.
Supplier access permits supported read integrations. Unavailable interfaces remain manual exceptions.
Structured requests are sufficient for the pilot, so no model loop is needed.
The small spreadsheet prior does not justify making a workbook the main pricing method.
GDPR applies to customer profiles and accessibility details. EU AI Act duties apply if AI is later introduced; national rules govern relevant employee consultation.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one reservation interface and a small supplier set.
Customer acceptance does not itself create a reservation or authorise charges beyond the accepted terms.
unknowns: Which suppliers and fare types are supported by the current reservation system?
Which supplier interfaces are licensed and available?
Are quotes binding, indicative or subject to immediate repricing?
Which fees and currencies require calculation outside the main pricing engine?
What accessibility information is reliable enough to promise?
Who may approve unusual itineraries, discounts or risky connections?
What access, supplier agreements and employee consultation are needed?
research_questions: Which supported interfaces return all-in prices, quote expiry and cancellation terms?
How should connections across separate tickets be distinguished from protected connections?
How can inventory freshness and currency rounding be validated before quote delivery?
new_work: Maintain supplier adapters, fee schedules and connection rules.
Handle unsupported inventory and incomplete accessibility information.
Review unusual itinerary trade-offs and fare exceptions.
Reprice expired quotes and explain changes to customers.
Monitor failed integrations and reconcile supplier pricing discrepancies.
tasks.statement: Plan routes, itineraries, and accommodation details, and compute fares and fees, using schedules, rate books, and computers.

tasks.short: Make and confirm transportation and accommodation reservations.

steps.what: Read the travel request and identify booking details.

loop.input: Travel request and confirmed travel requirements.
loop.output: Structured booking details with source passages and missing fields.
loop.check: Validate dates, passenger counts and locations; agent verifies extracted facts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one correction attempt; unresolved fields return to the agent.
loop.why_not_simpler: Requests contain free text. Structured requests bypass the loop.

steps.what: Search availability and fares in reservation system {OTHER}.
Discuss trade-offs and agree an itinerary with the customer.
Enter passenger details and create a provisional hold in reservation system {OTHER}.
Check final terms and commit the booking in reservation system {OTHER}.
Send the booking confirmation and travel documents.

tasks.design: A {WORKFLOW} intake validates booking details and queries the reservation system {OTHER}; a bounded extraction loop handles free-text requests from {EMAIL}. Existing reservation controls create permitted holds, require agent approval before commitment, and send confirmations through {EMAIL} after successful booking.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier access, changing fares and duplicate entry between requests and reservation records made the connections costly. Many booking functions already exist.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reservation controls handle transactions. AI-assisted coding lowers the effort of building adapters, validation rules and confirmation templates.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier interfaces differ. Inventory can change between quote and commitment, and partial failures need careful recovery.
tasks.human_edge: Explain real trade-offs, negotiate alternatives and protect customers whose needs do not fit standard fare rules.

ambition.what: A connection-risk review for complex itineraries before ticket commitment.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from rekeying bookings to handling difficult itineraries and failed transactions. No new commercial decision rights arise unless fare and rebooking limits are delegated.

reach.task: Prepare alternatives when a confirmed journey is disrupted.
reach.learn: Disruption policies, connection constraints and the limits of rebooking authority.

evidence.claim: Existing lodging software supports customer self-service and automated operational steps; this does not establish transport-booking coverage.
Free-text transaction extraction with master-data checks and exception routing exists in order management.
Reservation holds, fare validation and confirmation generation can use deterministic transaction logic where interfaces permit.

assumptions: The setting is a customer-facing travel or transport business with 200 to 2,000 staff.
Travel requirements are established upstream; this task covers booking execution.
Only reversible, fee-free holds run without agent approval.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Access work includes GDPR controls and employee consultation under applicable national rules.
unknowns: Which reservation and supplier interfaces permit searches, holds and commitments?
Which bookings require payment before confirmation?
What fare limits and commitment authority do agents currently have?
Which national employee consultation requirements apply?
research_questions: Can supplier operations be retried without creating duplicate bookings?
Can final prices and cancellation terms be checked immediately before commitment?
new_work: Review extracted booking details and commitment previews.
Recover expired holds, partial bookings and failed confirmations.
Maintain supplier mappings, fare checks and retry rules.
tasks.statement: Make and confirm reservations for transportation and accommodations, using telephones, faxes, mail, and computers.

tasks.short: Prepare customer invoices and take payment.

steps.what: Retrieve billable booking details from reservation system {OTHER}.
Enter billing details and generate the invoice.
Check invoice totals and approve billing exceptions within delegated limits.
Send the customer invoice and payment instructions.
Take customer-authorised payment through payment terminal {OTHER}.
Record the payment reference and issue the receipt.

tasks.design: An integration transfers booking charges from the reservation system {OTHER} into configured invoice templates and billing rules in {ERP}. {WORKFLOW} routes billing exceptions for approval, sends a payment request through {EMAIL}, and records authenticated results from the payment service {OTHER} before issuing a receipt.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most capabilities already exist, but booking references, invoice lines and payment references may not be connected. Billing exceptions discourage unattended processing.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured invoicing and customer-authorised payment flows cover the standard path. AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of mappings and reliable payment-event handling.
tasks.still_hard: Travel tax treatment, deposits, split payments and failed transactions need precise rules. Cash payments retain physical handling.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve disputed charges and explain payment problems without pressuring the customer.
tasks.altitude: Routine invoice preparation and payment posting largely leave the agent's week. The agent handles billing exceptions within existing limits; financial approval rights do not change.

reach.task: Investigate unmatched payments before a booking deadline expires.
reach.learn: Payment statuses, duplicate prevention, settlement timing and escalation limits.

evidence.claim: Existing lodging software provides automatic charge routing; this supports part of the proposed billing flow.
Invoice calculations, payment references and authenticated payment-event processing can use deterministic rules.

assumptions: The baseline includes counter card payments; online payment links can replace agent handling for suitable customers.
The customer's authorisation remains required even when agent handling falls to zero.
Standard invoices pass fixed checks; the human gate applies to billing exceptions.
Exceptions beyond agent limits go to the finance team.
Time estimates exclude payment processing fees and assume no material cash-payment workload.
Access estimates include GDPR controls and any consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Can booking charges be exported with stable invoice references?
What share of payments is cash, card, bank transfer or split payment?
Which tax treatments and billing exceptions occur?
Which payment and invoice corrections require finance approval?
research_questions: Can existing configuration connect invoices and payment results without custom code?
How are duplicate events, reversals and interrupted payments handled?
new_work: Review billing exceptions and disputed amounts.
Investigate unmatched, reversed and duplicate payment events.
Maintain charge mappings, tax rules and payment credentials.
tasks.statement: Prepare customer invoices and accept payment.

tasks.short: Answer questions about schedules, accommodations, procedures and policies.

steps.what: Read the inquiry and identify the question and relevant booking.

loop.input: Customer inquiry and an approved list of inquiry types.
loop.output: Inquiry type, extracted search fields or a handover reason.
loop.check: Require an allowed type and valid fields; verify identity separately before private record access.
loop.stop: One classification attempt; ambiguous, unsupported or incomplete requests go to an agent.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text questions vary. Menu selections and exact matches bypass the loop.

steps.what: Check live schedules, availability or booking facts in reservation system {OTHER}.
Find the applicable procedure or policy.
Prepare an answer using the travel facts and applicable policy.
Check and send the routine answer.
Discuss uncertain answers, special circumstances or policy exceptions with the customer.

tasks.design: An answer desk in {HELPDESK} classifies free-text inquiries, retrieves live facts from the reservation system {OTHER}, and selects versioned policies from {DOCS}. Deterministic templates send supported answers through {EMAIL}; missing facts, conflicting policies and requests for exceptions reach a reservation agent with the evidence attached.
tasks.previous_blocker: Answers combine live travel data with policies held elsewhere. Static answers become unreliable when schedules or conditions change.
tasks.enabler_now: Maintained knowledge articles, live lookups and existing routing cover the standard path. A bounded classifier handles varied wording without generating unrestricted policy advice.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent disruption questions and contradictory supplier information need people. Accurate policy ownership and live-data freshness remain ongoing costs.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise distress, explain uncertainty and negotiate a practical next step when the published answer is insufficient.

ambition.what: After-hours customers seeking routine schedule and procedure information.

tasks.altitude: The agent handles fewer repeated questions and more uncertain journeys and policy exceptions. Existing escalation and exception-approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Maintain approved answers for recurring travel questions.
reach.learn: Policy versioning, source attribution, plain-language writing and handover criteria.

evidence.claim: Knowledge-base answering with a pre-filled request when an answer is unavailable exists today.
Customer-question automation can use integrations to retrieve records and perform supported actions.
Customer-facing AI interactions require applicable transparency disclosures.
Live lookups and approved answer templates can serve supported travel inquiries without free-form generation.

assumptions: The baseline combines written inquiries with telephone handling of complex cases.
Lookup steps apply when the question needs those sources; shares average across the inquiry mix.
Automatic answers use approved templates, current sources and validated fields.
A failed source check or unsupported question triggers human handover.
Customer-facing AI is disclosed, and GDPR access and retention controls apply.
Time estimates are unmeasured; access estimates include consultation under applicable national rules.
unknowns: What proportion of inquiries has a stable, approved answer?
Which live schedule and booking interfaces are available?
Who approves policy wording and handles conflicting supplier advice?
What after-hours human escalation service exists?
Which employee consultation requirements apply to routing or reporting changes?
research_questions: How accurately can supported questions be separated from questions needing human judgement?
What freshness limits prevent outdated schedule or policy answers?
Can current configuration provide sufficient routing before custom classification is built?
new_work: Maintain approved answers, source dates and policy versions.
Handle unsupported inquiries and failed live-data checks.
Sample sent answers for incorrect routing and stale facts.
Review handover delays and update supported inquiry types.
tasks.statement: Answer inquiries regarding information, such as schedules, accommodations, procedures, or policies.

tasks.short: Issue authorised tickets and insurance documents, assemble itineraries and deliver the travel pack.

steps.what: Retrieve the booking, passenger details and purchased services from the reservation system.
Check names, itinerary, payment status and recorded traveller authorisation against issuance requirements.
Issue transport tickets in the ticketing system after resolving validation exceptions.
Request the traveller's selected insurance policy through the supplier portal.
Assemble tickets, policies, itinerary and joining instructions into a travel pack.
Send the travel pack to the confirmed recipient.

tasks.design: Use the reservation and ticketing system {OTHER} to validate structured booking data and prepare issuance actions, with separate approval before ticket or policy commitments take effect. A deterministic generator assembles issued documents from the {OTHER} and {PARTNER_PORTAL} into a versioned travel pack in the {DOCS}, then the {EMAIL} sends a secure link to the confirmed recipient. Role-based access and retention settings support GDPR requirements.
tasks.previous_blocker: Booking data, supplier issuance and document assembly sit across separate interfaces, with manual checks preventing costly mistakes.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing issuance features, reusable templates and smaller integration components can remove copying without changing supplier authority.
tasks.still_hard: Name mismatches, unusual fares, supplier outages, insurance permissions and irreversible issuance require careful exception handling.
tasks.human_edge: Explain restrictive terms, resolve conflicting traveller details and verify informed instructions before financial commitments.

ambition.what: Versioned travel packs refreshed after confirmed itinerary changes.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from assembling attachments to resolving booking and policy exceptions. The agent can correct presentation errors within delegated limits; commercial commitments still require the relevant issuance approval.

reach.task: Handle document corrections after a confirmed itinerary change.
reach.learn: Learn document versioning, fare restrictions and the boundary between correction and reissue.

evidence.claim: Structured booking data and fixed templates can generate itineraries and assemble issued documents deterministically.
Existing ticketing and supplier interfaces can support issuance, subject to contractual permissions and local capabilities.

assumptions: The traveller has already chosen the services and explicitly authorised purchase.
Insurance work means requesting an authorised supplier policy, not generating policy terms or selecting cover.
Standard bookings have structured issuance rules; unfamiliar terms enter a human exception queue.
Document-heavy work mainly concerns outputs, so the document-input prior does not justify a model loop.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.
Consultation under national rules, where applicable, is included in access planning.
unknowns: Which issuance actions can existing configuration support?
What supplier permissions and insurance distribution responsibilities apply?
Where are traveller authorisation and confirmed recipient details recorded?
Which GDPR retention periods, access controls and national consultation duties apply?
How often do unusual terms require manual interpretation?
research_questions: Can issuance retries safely detect an existing ticket or policy before submitting again?
Can one booking version bind validation, issuance and document assembly?
Which supplier documents must be preserved unchanged in the travel pack?
new_work: Resolve validation failures and unusual fare or policy conditions.
Check uncertain issuance outcomes before retrying.
Maintain templates, supplier mappings and issuance rules.
Handle failed delivery and revoke superseded document links.
Review access and retention settings.
tasks.statement: Assemble and issue required documentation, such as tickets, travel insurance policies, or itineraries.

tasks.short: Check travel availability and allocate the customer's chosen space.

steps.what: Capture dates, passenger details and preferences in the {OTHER} reservation system.
Check live capacity and allocation restrictions in the {OTHER} reservation system.
Explain available options and agree alternatives when requested spaces are unavailable.
Allocate the agreed space in the {OTHER} reservation system after customer approval.

tasks.design: Configure structured intake, availability filters and allocation rules in the {OTHER} reservation system. Recheck inventory when committing the customer's approved selection, prevent duplicate allocations and pass the reservation record to the confirmation workflow.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing booking functions may cover availability, but intake, supplier inventories and allocation rules are often configured separately.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reservation controls can handle the structured work. AI-assisted coding makes missing adapters cheaper to build; it does not create supplier access.
tasks.still_hard: Supplier inventory can change between search and commitment. Group allocations, accessibility requirements and inconsistent supplier restrictions need exception handling.
tasks.human_edge: Understand what the customer can compromise on when the requested journey is unavailable.

ambition.what: Flexible-date alternatives during the first customer contact

tasks.altitude: The agent spends less time searching and entering allocations, and more time resolving constrained journeys. They can offer approved alternatives immediately; pricing and compensation rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve unavailable-booking inquiries using approved alternatives.
reach.learn: Inventory freshness, allocation restrictions and the limits of a temporary hold.

evidence.claim: Structured availability checks and allocations can use deterministic reservation controls.
Mews supports hotel self-service and automated charge routing, adjacent to this reservation workflow.

assumptions: The baseline is a staffed travel desk using an existing reservation system.
That system supports live searches, configured allocation rules and safe commitment.
The structured-input prior fits this task; API availability remains unconfirmed.
Customer approval covers the exact selection and any disclosed commitment.
Time shares, remaining time and build ranges are planning estimates for one reservation-system connection.
GDPR applies to passenger records. Access and any employee consultation under national rules are included in consent_and_access.
unknowns: Whether the desk books transport, lodging or both.
Which inventory sources expose supported search and allocation interfaces.
Whether holds, duplicate prevention and atomic allocation are supported.
How often group requests or accessibility constraints require intervention.
Which configuration rights and national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which existing configuration can replace manual searching without new code?
How does the reservation interface handle expired availability, retries and partial group allocations?
new_work: Handle stale inventory and failed allocations.
Maintain allocation restrictions and supplier mappings.
Check duplicate prevention and inventory freshness after interface changes.
tasks.statement: Determine whether space is available on travel dates requested by customers, assigning requested spaces when available.

tasks.short: Explain travel times, connections and applicable visa or health requirements using current, authoritative information.

steps.what: Clarify the itinerary, traveller circumstances and information needed.
Look up departure times and connections in the reservation system.
Consult official visa and health guidance and approved travel requirements.
Determine applicable requirements and identify questions needing specialist advice.
Prepare a clear explanation of travel facts and reviewed requirements.

loop.input: Travel facts, human-reviewed requirements and dated authoritative source excerpts.
loop.output: A plain-language travel advice draft with source references and unresolved questions.
loop.check: Check dates, times and destinations against structured facts; require source support for every requirement and human review.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction attempt; missing or stale evidence returns an approved template and a referral.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard facts, but mixed traveller questions need a short explanation of already-reviewed information.

steps.what: Explain the advice, answer follow-up questions and refer uncertain visa or health matters.
Record the advice and any follow-up in the customer case.

tasks.design: A deterministic answer desk retrieves schedules from the reservation system in {OTHER} and approved, dated requirement sources from {GOV_PORTAL} and {DOCS}. A bounded loop drafts explanations from those facts and the agent's reviewed requirements; the agent approves personalised advice before delivery, and the {WORKFLOW} records it in the {HELPDESK}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Travel facts and entry guidance came from different sources with different update cycles. A fluent answer was not enough to establish that a requirement applied to a particular traveller.
tasks.enabler_now: Controlled retrieval, freshness checks and short drafting loops can reduce searching and rewriting. Existing knowledge and case features provide much of the structure.
tasks.still_hard: Transit rules, nationality, residency and individual health questions can change the answer. Official guidance may be ambiguous or stale; personal medical advice requires a qualified professional.
tasks.human_edge: Ask the missing question, recognise uncertainty and help the traveller understand consequences without promising entry or giving medical advice.

ambition.what: A pre-departure requirements briefing for multi-country itineraries.

tasks.altitude: The agent spends more time clarifying difficult journeys and less time searching or rewriting standard information. The briefing is a new service; authority to determine entry eligibility or give medical advice does not change.

reach.task: Prepare written follow-up advice with dated source references.
reach.learn: Learn source attribution, plain-language writing and how to preserve uncertainty.

reach.task: Track unresolved travel questions through specialist referral.
reach.learn: Learn case ownership, referral criteria and follow-up deadlines.

evidence.claim: TOPdesk Robin answers from a knowledge base and creates a pre-filled request when it cannot answer.
Zendesk AI agents answer customer questions through integrated channels; this supports the answer-desk pattern, not visa or medical accuracy.
The NBER support-agent study found productivity gains from an assistant. It does not establish savings for travel-requirement advice.
A customer-facing AI chatbot must disclose that the user is interacting with AI.
Applying travel requirements to unusual circumstances needs authoritative evidence and human judgement.

assumptions: The company provides travel information rather than regulated medical or immigration advice.
Approved source links can be indexed without indiscriminate copying of entire government sites.
A model drafts explanations; it does not invent requirements or decide eligibility.
The high error-cost prior supports a gate on personalised advice, while retrieval and paperwork remain open to automation.
GDPR applies to traveller context. Health details are collected only when necessary and handled under an appropriate legal basis.
EU AI Act transparency duties apply if a customer-facing AI channel is added. National rules may require employee consultation.
Time shares and build ranges are estimates for one service desk and a limited set of destinations.
unknowns: Which sources are approved and who maintains them?
Which traveller details may the company collect and retain?
What advice may agents give under their training and insurance arrangements?
Which questions must go to a carrier, consulate or qualified health professional?
Does the company already record advice and source dates?
Which languages, destinations and consultation requirements must the pilot cover?
research_questions: Which authoritative sources provide update dates or change notices suitable for freshness checks?
How reliably can drafts preserve qualifications and distinguish destination rules from transit rules?
What referral wording helps travellers act when official guidance is incomplete?
new_work: Review personalised requirement advice before delivery.
Maintain approved sources, expiry rules and referral routes.
Check drafts for unsupported claims and missing qualifications.
Handle conflicting or unavailable source information.
Maintain case retention and access rules for sensitive traveller details.
tasks.statement: Inform clients of essential travel information, such as travel times, transportation connections, or medical and visa requirements.

tasks.short: Maintain passenger-space inventory and provide current availability.

steps.what: Inspect reservations, holds and available space in the reservation system.
Compare partner allotments against the reservation inventory.
Agree corrections for disputed counts, holds or allotments.
Enter authorised blocks, releases and corrections in the reservation system.
Tell passengers or colleagues how much space remains.

tasks.design: Configure a live availability view in the reservation system {OTHER}; a connector compares permitted allotment data from the {PARTNER_PORTAL} and queues discrepancies in the {WORKFLOW}. Validated allocation requests and approved corrections update the {OTHER} with capacity checks, duplicate protection and an audit trail. Structured availability answers use the same inventory version and show when it was last confirmed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Booking transactions already update inventory automatically, but partner allotments and exceptional corrections often cross separate interfaces.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing inventory controls can be configured, while AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building adapters and reconciliation checks.
tasks.still_hard: Concurrent sales, expired holds, delayed partner updates and disputed capacity require reliable transaction controls and operational decisions.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve competing claims on scarce capacity and recognise when a technically valid allocation would cause an operational problem.

ambition.what: Review expiring group holds before each release deadline.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from checking counts and rekeying changes to resolving allocation conflicts. Within delegated limits, the agent can release expired holds without waiting for a weekly reconciliation.

reach.task: Review capacity exceptions and release priorities.
reach.learn: Understand allotment contracts, hold deadlines and delegated capacity limits.

evidence.claim: Capacity checks, hold expiry and structured inventory reconciliation can use deterministic rules.
Order imports and stock synchronisation demonstrate an adjacent integration pattern, not passenger-inventory capability.

assumptions: The setting includes partner allotments and occasional manual inventory corrections.
Ordinary booking transactions already update inventory; the proposal addresses remaining clerk work.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
The structured-input prior supports rules and integration; a language model adds little here.
Access effort excludes any extended consultation process required by national rules.
unknowns: Which reservation interfaces support versioned reads, conditional writes and hold expiry?
Which source is authoritative when partner and internal counts differ?
What allocation decisions may the agent make without controller approval?
What access approvals and consultation under national rules apply?
research_questions: Can existing reservation configuration remove the need for a custom reconciliation connector?
How does the interface prevent duplicate updates and overselling during concurrent transactions?
new_work: Investigate stale feeds and unmatched allotments.
Review disputed capacity corrections.
Maintain identifier mappings, hold rules and delegated limits.
Monitor failed writes and reconcile after outages.
tasks.statement: Maintain computerized inventories of available passenger space and provide information on space reserved or available.

tasks.short: Discuss customer requirements and travel preferences.

steps.what: Read the customer profile and previous travel preferences.
Discuss purpose, budget, timing, flexibility and practical travel needs.
Turn conversation notes into a draft requirements summary.

loop.input: Agent-written conversation notes and a fixed requirements schema.
loop.output: Draft requirements with priorities, uncertainties and source passages.
loop.check: Agent checks meaning, missing needs and unsupported inferences; schema validates fields.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction attempt; agent completes unresolved fields.
loop.why_not_simpler: Narrative notes express priorities and qualifications that fixed field mappings cannot reliably recover.

steps.what: Confirm priorities and resolve conflicting requirements with the customer.
Save confirmed requirements against the customer record.

tasks.design: A configured {CRM} view presents relevant customer context and a short requirements form. A bounded loop turns agent-written notes into a draft for review, then {WORKFLOW} saves the customer-confirmed requirements and creates the booking brief without duplicate entry.
tasks.previous_blocker: The difficult part is discovering priorities through conversation. Notes and customer records often use different structures.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms cover fixed facts, while a small model loop can structure narrative notes. AI-assisted coding makes the record connection cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Customers may be uncertain or reveal conflicting needs. Accessibility and health-related details require careful, limited handling.
tasks.human_edge: Build trust, hear hesitation and help customers make trade-offs they can accept.

ambition.what: A customer-confirmed accessibility brief that travels with the booking.

tasks.altitude: The agent spends less time rewriting notes and more time clarifying difficult needs. Recommendation quality improves, but booking and pricing authority do not change.

reach.task: Prepare arrival assistance from confirmed practical requirements.
reach.learn: Accessible-service arrangements, minimal information sharing and escalation routes.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, requirements summaries and record updates can support a human travel-preference conversation.
A documented support-assistant study found productivity gains, but does not establish gains for travel-preference interviews.

assumptions: The baseline is an assisted telephone consultation; counter consultations follow similar boundaries.
The loop uses typed notes rather than new call recording.
Only necessary practical requirements are retained, with appropriate GDPR handling.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Access estimates include employee consultation where national rules require it.
unknowns: Where are customer preferences currently stored?
Which practical requirements must suppliers receive?
What lawful basis, retention periods and access restrictions apply to sensitive details?
Does the employer already record calls or consult employees about these tools?
research_questions: Does a short structured form remove enough rewriting to make the model loop unnecessary?
Can summary review detect omitted qualifications without lengthening the consultation?
new_work: Check summaries for omitted priorities and invented assumptions.
Remove outdated preferences and unnecessary sensitive details.
Maintain requirements fields and supplier handoff formats.
tasks.statement: Confer with customers to determine their service requirements and travel preferences.

tasks.short: Check passenger documents and booking details, resolve discrepancies, assign seats and issue boarding passes.

steps.what: Ask the passenger for a booking reference and travel documents.
Read document fields and retrieve the booking in the departure-control system.
Check identity, destination and required documents; resolve discrepancies before clearing the passenger.
Assign an available seat and issue the boarding pass in the departure-control system.
Hand over the boarding pass and explain where and when to board.

tasks.design: Configure document reading, booking lookup and seat assignment in the departure-control system in {OTHER}, with deterministic checks for missing fields and mismatches. A reservation agent records passenger clearance before the system issues a boarding pass; unclear documents and adverse decisions go to a person, while standard passes and directions are delivered automatically.
tasks.previous_blocker: The difficult part was document interpretation and carrier responsibility, rather than data entry alone. Scanner support, clearance rules and boarding-pass issuance were often disconnected.
tasks.enabler_now: Machine-readable documents and existing departure-control features can handle routine lookup and issuance. AI-assisted coding makes small adapters and exception displays cheaper; it does not establish document authenticity.
tasks.still_hard: Identity matching, unusual documents, minors and changing entry conditions require care. Carrier permission, authoritative rules and reliable clearance records are essential.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise mismatches, understand unusual circumstances and explain a document problem without treating a failed scan as a refusal.

ambition.what: Assisted check-in for passengers unable to use self-service document scanning.

tasks.altitude: The agent spends less time copying fields and more time helping passengers with document or accessibility problems. Clearance and escalation rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve passenger booking mismatches before departure.
reach.learn: Learn booking identifiers, correction limits and escalation routes.

reach.task: Diagnose document-reader and boarding-pass delivery failures.
reach.learn: Learn device diagnostics and how to report faults without copying identity documents.

evidence.claim: Machine-readable document fields, booking lookup and seat allocation can use deterministic processing; authenticity and unusual requirements remain harder.
Mews offers online check-in and kiosks for hotels. This is adjacent evidence for self-service intake, not proof of transport document clearance.
GDPR Article 22 restricts solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects; automated adverse travel decisions need separate assessment.

assumptions: This task occurs at a transport departure counter using a departure-control system in {OTHER}.
Routine documents have machine-readable fields; unreadable documents fall back to assisted handling.
The passenger authorises ordinary check-in, and issuance requires a recorded human clearance.
No model decides document authenticity, entry eligibility or boarding refusal.
Time shares are planning estimates. The automation prior overstates what software alone can do when identity checks matter.
GDPR requires limited access and retention. EU AI Act duties apply to any AI added; national rules govern relevant employee consultation.
Build ranges cover one carrier or departure-control interface, not a multi-carrier rollout.
unknowns: Which document-reading and self-service features are already licensed?
Does the departure-control interface expose clearance flags and safe issuance controls?
Which checks require a trained agent under carrier procedures?
Who handles document exceptions and boarding refusals?
Which document fields may be retained, and for how long?
What employee consultation and device access are required?
research_questions: Which supported document formats can be read without a generative model?
How should issuance be retried without duplicate passes or conflicting seat assignments?
Which carrier rules require inspection of the original document?

tasks.statement: Examine passenger documentation to determine destinations and to assign boarding passes.

tasks.short: Help passengers who need assistance board or leave transport safely.

steps.what: Read the assistance request in the reservation system {OTHER}.
Meet the passenger and confirm their preferred assistance.
Assess the route, equipment and conditions before moving.
Coordinate the boarding or disembarking handover with transport staff.
Assist the passenger physically and complete the agreed handover.
Record completion and exceptions in the reservation system {OTHER}.

tasks.design: Configure the reservation system {OTHER} to pass minimum necessary assistance details into a mobile queue in the {WORKFLOW}. Staff acknowledge handovers and confirm prefilled completion records, while missed acknowledgements trigger notifications. Passenger conversations, route checks and physical assistance remain with trained people.
tasks.previous_blocker: Assistance details, departure changes and staff handovers sit in separate operational channels. Much of the task requires physical presence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing queues, forms and notifications can remove repeated coordination where interfaces are available. AI-assisted coding can make a small connector cheaper to build.
tasks.still_hard: Live conditions, equipment availability, passenger comfort and reliable handovers require trained staff and local knowledge.
tasks.human_edge: Respect the passenger's autonomy, adapt assistance in the moment and recognise unsafe conditions.
tasks.altitude: Most of the week and all safety decision rights stay the same. Staff spend slightly less time locating requests and recording completed assistance.

reach.task: Coordinate recovery when assistance handovers are missed.
reach.learn: Capacity planning, escalation thresholds and transport-provider responsibilities.

evidence.claim: Structured requests, acknowledgements and completion records can use deterministic workflow automation.
Software coordination does not replace physical assistance or on-site safety judgement.
Assistance records may reveal health information and require appropriate GDPR safeguards and processing conditions.

Staff have required training and equipment.
The future uses operational acknowledgements rather than employee performance scoring.

tasks.statement: Provide boarding or disembarking assistance to passengers needing special assistance.

tasks.short: Announce confirmed arrivals, departures and movement changes through public-address equipment.

steps.what: Read arrival, departure and location updates in the transport operations system.
Confirm changed or unclear movement details with operations staff.
Prepare announcement wording using the approved phrase sheet.
Broadcast arrival and departure information through the public-address console.

tasks.design: Feed confirmed movement data from the transport operations system {OTHER} into approved templates and recorded phrases in the public-address system {OTHER}. tasks.enabler_now: Existing announcement features can provide templates, recorded phrases and release controls; a small deterministic connector supplies movement facts.
tasks.still_hard: Last-minute changes, conflicting instructions, pronunciation, audibility and correct zone selection need operational testing.
tasks.human_edge: Notice passenger confusion, interpret urgent instructions and choose when a live clarification is necessary.
tasks.altitude: The agent spends less time composing and speaking routine announcements and more time helping passengers interpret changes. No new operational decision rights are assumed.

reach.task: Coordinate announcements during service disruption.
reach.learn: Learn escalation protocols, zone priorities and accessible passenger communication.

evidence.claim: Approved phrases populated from structured movement data can automate routine announcement preparation without a language model.
Public-address integration and intelligibility require local validation; the digest provides no direct deployment case.

The estimates cover routine movement announcements; emergency command remains a separate procedure.
Time shares and remaining time are planning estimates.

tasks.short: Recommend and promote destinations, tour packages and travel services.

steps.what: Ask customers about budget, interests, dates and practical constraints.
Compare suitable packages in the {OTHER} reservation system against customer requirements.
Explain package trade-offs and respond to customer concerns.
Draft a tailored package summary in the {EMAIL}.

loop.input: Approved package facts, current terms and agent-entered customer preferences.
loop.output: A short package summary with references to supplied facts.
loop.check: Validate prices, dates, inclusions and links against supplied records; the agent checks suitability before sending.
loop.stop: One draft and at most one repair within 30 seconds; use a fixed template or manual draft on failure.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates remain the default. A bounded drafting loop handles explanations tailored to free-text concerns without maintaining many template variants.

steps.what: Check claims, prices and contact permission, then send the summary through the {EMAIL}.
Record customer interest and follow-up actions in the {CRM}.

tasks.design: Configure package filters in the {OTHER} reservation system and concise preference capture in the {CRM}. Generate factual summaries from templates, using a bounded drafting loop only for tailored explanations, and require agent approval before sending through the {EMAIL}. Create follow-up tasks from the recorded customer response and permitted contact purpose.
tasks.previous_blocker: Catalogue facts and customer preferences are separated, while tailored explanations take writing time. Software can filter packages but cannot establish customer trust.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured filters handle factual matching. Bounded drafting can turn approved facts and customer concerns into an editable summary.
tasks.still_hard: Travel suitability depends on unstated expectations. Availability, package claims and contact permissions must remain current.
tasks.human_edge: Discover what matters to the traveller and explain trade-offs without pressuring them into an unsuitable purchase.

ambition.what: Written trade-off summary for undecided travellers

tasks.altitude: The agent spends more time advising and less time searching or composing follow-ups. They gain discretion over how to explain approved packages, while discounts and package terms retain existing approval limits.

reach.task: Prepare travel follow-ups from approved package facts.
reach.learn: Package inclusions, claim verification and permitted contact purposes.

evidence.claim: Deterministic filters can shortlist packages using dates, budget and explicit requirements.
bol's Shophulp provides conversational product advice; the digest identifies it as a beta, not a travel-advice case.
Drafting a reply from a case record with clerk approval is an established assistive pattern.

Package facts and prices are available in structured records.
The relationship and low-rule-coverage priors fit the advisory conversation; factual shortlisting is more structured.

Time shares and build ranges are planning estimates for a limited package catalogue.

Sample drafts for unsupported claims and maintain the bounded drafting instructions.
tasks.statement: Promote particular destinations, tour packages, and other travel services.

tasks.short: Help travellers prepare required travel documents and forms.

steps.what: Clarify the journey and collect traveller details.
Check official requirements for the traveller and itinerary.
Inspect supplied documents and identify missing or inconsistent details.

loop.input: Traveller documents and the required field schema.
loop.output: Extracted fields, source locations and unreadable-field flags.

loop.stop: One extraction and one retry per document; unreadable or conflicting fields go to the reservation agent.

Explain missing items and resolve questions about completing the forms.
Review the completed forms with the traveller and obtain required signatures.

A bounded extraction loop reads supplied documents; deterministic mappings generate forms in the {DOCS} after field verification. The traveller approves declarations and signatures, with submission kept separate from preparation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document formats vary, official requirements change, and forms often require repeated entry across disconnected channels.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing forms and document tools cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding can reduce the cost of field mappings and validation, while bounded extraction handles varied scans.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping requirements current, interpreting unusual circumstances and supporting official forms without stable interfaces remain expensive.
tasks.human_edge: Explain uncertain requirements calmly, notice inconsistencies and recognise when the traveller needs an official authority or specialist.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from copying details to resolving document exceptions and offering readiness reviews. The agent gains no authority to determine entry eligibility or sign traveller declarations.

reach.learn: Plain-language correspondence, approved wording and secure document handling.

GDPR requires a lawful basis, limited collection and appropriate protection for traveller documents.

tasks.short: Suggest travel options and provide useful guides, maps and information sources.

Compare suitable options against the traveller's preferences.
Assemble selected suggestions, guides and maps for the traveller.
Explain the suggestions and answer the traveller's follow-up questions.

tasks.short: Confirm reservations and tell customers or travel agents about transport changes.

tasks.short: Obtain current supplier brochures and maintain a usable travel-information library.

Email routine requests for replacement brochures to supplier contacts.
Call suppliers to chase missing material or arrange printed copies.

tasks.short: Keep the information desk and customer area clean during service.
